explanation: The full two-sample scanpy preprocessing/clustering workflow completed offline under the controller in 147.5 s (600 s budget) with peak child RSS ~5.18 GiB (8 GiB budget), exit code 0, from a fresh working/output directory with the controller-appended exports. All three declared artifacts were produced: cell_clusters_umap.csv (1,098,166 bytes; 17,041 cells), rank_genes_groups_leiden_res_0.50.csv (28,207,516 bytes), rank_genes_groups_params.json. The input-staging recipe verified both 10x .h5 files against the figshare provider md5/size records and wrote the pooch registry; the controller's post-run verify-staging re-hashed all three declared input files and confirmed they stayed byte-identical. Reading the exported CSVs (no recomputation) confirms the notebook's own narrative: 8785+8340 cells and 36,601 genes read, 17,041 cells / 23,427 genes after the notebook's permissive filtering; leiden_res_0.02 yields exactly clusters 0-4 so the hardcoded lineage map annotates every cell (Lymphocytes 9763, Monocytes 1507, B Cells 2269, Erythroid 3502); leiden_res_0.50 yields 17 clusters and leiden_res_2.00 yields 36 (the over-clustered case the notebook describes); cluster 7's top DE genes are NKG7 and GNLY, matching the notebook's stated NK-cell finding; the DE params JSON records groupby=leiden_res_0.50, method=wilcoxon, reference=rest, corr_method=benjamini-hochberg. The dependency environment (scanpy 1.12.4, anndata 0.13.4, igraph 1.0.0, leidenalg 0.12.0, umap-learn 0.5.12, pooch 1.9.0, scikit-image 0.26.0, CPython 3.13.13) was installed by the controller from the recipe, and the same versions were used for pre-test import/headless-plotting checks. Headless rendering was verified: every plotting call in the source (violin, scatter, highly_variable_genes, pca_variance_ratio, pca, umap, dotplot, rank_genes_groups_dotplot) ran under Agg in the reference run and in a cheap synthetic-data environment check.
source_adaptations: analysis.py: selected matplotlib's non-interactive Agg backend (and the controller also sets MPLBACKEND=Agg) before scanpy imports pyplot, because the reference run is headless with no display. All plotting calls in the source are retained and still render off-screen; no figure, parameter or computation was changed.

analysis.py: pinned the pooch data cache to the persistent controller cache root by setting XDG_CACHE_HOME=/work/cache, so pooch.os_cache('scverse_tutorials') resolves to /work/cache/scverse_tutorials where the recipe stages the original dataset files, instead of the unreachable default user cache under $HOME. This is an input-path adaptation only: the same file names and bytes are read.

analysis.py: replaced EXAMPLE_DATA.load_registry_from_doi() with EXAMPLE_DATA.load_registry(pooch.os_cache('scverse_tutorials') / 'registry.txt'). Upstream, that call queries the figshare API over the network to learn the article's file names and md5 checksums for doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1; the reference environment is offline, so the identical registry (one '<name> md5:<provider_md5>' line per dataset file, built from that same provider metadata) is written into the cache by stage-inputs.sh and loaded from disk. Only that ambient network access is removed: pooch still resolves each cached file, verifies its md5 against this registry before returning it, and sc.read_10x_h5 then reads the original provider bytes.

stage-inputs.sh stages the two original 10x .h5 inputs into /work/cache/scverse_tutorials (the directory pooch.fetch resolves to) with size and md5 verification against the figshare article metadata, reusing the controller-staged copies under /inputs when they match and otherwise downloading from the provider's ndownloader URLs during setup. It also writes the pooch registry.txt described above. No scientific code, threshold, algorithm, seed or filtering rule was altered anywhere; the exports and endpoint inventory are untouched.
unresolved_assumptions: Exact-version reproducibility was not pinned: the recipe states minimum versions (from scanpy 1.12.4's own dependency set) rather than exact pins, and the controller resolved scanpy 1.12.4 / anndata 0.13.4 / numpy 2.5.4 / pandas 3.0.6 / scipy 1.18.1 / igraph 1.0.0. A future resolution with different versions could change UMAP coordinates or cluster labels, so the exported values should be treated as reproducible for this resolved environment only; the controller recorded the installed package set.

The igraph-flavored Leiden runs are internally deterministic in this scanpy version (no seed is passed downstream and igraph's RNG is reset after each call), but I did not verify bitwise identity across repeated executions, so run-to-run stability of the exported cluster labels is assumed rather than measured.

Dataset stability is assumed from the provider: the staged .h5 files matched the figshare article's published md5 and size records at staging time (and were re-verified unchanged by the controller after the run), but no independent second checksum of those files exists beyond the provider's own md5 records.

Timing/memory headroom beyond this run is not guaranteed: 147.5 s and ~5.18 GiB peak RSS were observed on this controller; a slower or more contended host could approach the 600 s / 8 GiB limits even though this run had ~4x time headroom.
